Social democratic parties emerged as a political force in the late 19th and early 20th centuries as a response to the social and economic upheavals caused by industrialization and rapid urbanization. These parties initially focused on advocating for workers' rights and improving their living and working conditions.

During the post-World War II period, social democratic parties experienced a period of electoral success and implemented a range of policies aimed at expanding the welfare state, promoting labor rights, and increasing economic equality. In recent years, social democratic parties have faced a range of challenges, including declining membership, loss of electoral support, and the rise of populist and far-right movements.
